_notes.purpose: Milldale is the engine's test world. Entirely fictional, entirely SFW, small enough to read in one sitting and wide enough to touch every schema feature the two prose renderers consume. Nothing here is drawn from anybody's life.
_notes.one_line_and_surface: The schema has no field for the roster line a bible prints per character, and no field for what a walled relative is allowed to be told about somebody. Added two: `one_line` (COMMONS text, read by anyone who can see the cast list at all) and `surface` (what an own_bible viewer gets instead). The renderer falls back to the first sentence of `voice` for `one_line`, and to a mechanical 'someone from <orbit>' for `surface`, because deriving a surface from `voice` would leak voice.
_notes.commons_discipline: one_line, place.description and week[].doing are commons text. Nothing a wall protects is authored into them. Dale's Thursday slot says the basement door is closed; it does not say what is behind it. That is the whole trick.
_notes.canon_rule_objects: canon_rules and texture are documented as arrays of strings. Rating-gating one needs somewhere to hang rating_min, so the renderer accepts either a bare string or {text, rating_min}. Both forms appear below.
_notes.economy_labels_and_rules: economies[] has no display label and no prose earn rules in the doc, only the machine token list `earned_by`. Added optional `label` and `rules`; the renderer humanizes `earned_by` tokens when `rules` is absent.
_notes.subconscious_flag: The doc types `framing` as prose. The renderer treats an explicit boolean `subconscious` as authoritative and otherwise sniffs the word 'subconscious' out of `framing`. casserole_ledger uses the prose form; thursday_pot is deliberately NOT subconscious, so both paths get exercised.
_notes.secret_visibility: gossip_grade decides whether a secret reaches the shared bible at all. A secret with gossip_grade:false renders only for its owner and for the narrator; the doc left this to the renderer.
_notes.special_role_name: The doc lists spouse|boss|parent|pastor as example roles. Roles are free-form relationship nouns; Janelle's is 'child'.
_notes.same_entity_link: A person can exist twice in a world — once as scenery on a shift, once as somebody you talk to. `harlan_counter` is that case on purpose: `same_as` is the same-entity link, and the renderers dedupe on it so Harlan does not walk through the bible under two names.
_notes.days: week[].days and fixtures[].days use 0=Sunday through 6=Saturday, matching PHP's 'w' and the doc's [1,3,5] weekday examples.
_notes.rating_test_hook: This world's ceiling is sfw. Harlan's drive carries rating_min 'mature' purely so the test suite has a node to watch vanish; its content is a man's money worry, which is what 'mature' means in a wholesome world.
_notes.the_child: Theo is twelve and he is an ordinary member of this cast: a schedule, an orbit, a room he is in every weekday, a dossier, a portrait, and the one secret in Milldale that a mystery would be built on. He is here because a town with no children is not a town, and because a child seeing something nobody believes is the oldest working part in the genre. The only thing his age changes is that he is not in the desire economy — no flirt_style, no attraction_seeds, and xeric_effective_rating() holds him at sfw in a world of any rating. That exclusion is the engine modelling something true, the same way the walls do.

meta.name: Milldale
meta.description: A river town of nine hundred, a church basement, and a mill nobody goes into.
meta.author: xeric

occupation.title: retired line foreman
occupation.hours: none, and he has not gotten used to it

goals.text: get through the winter without asking Janelle for anything
keep showing up to things after his wife stopped being the reason he went

setting.locale: a river town of nine hundred in southern Ohio
texture: coffee that has been on the burner since six
a river you can smell before you can see it
church bells three minutes fast since 1974
canon_rules: The diner closes at two and does not reopen for anyone.
Nobody on Chapel Street locks a door, and nobody says why.

canon_rules.text: The mill gate stays chained. It has been chained since the year it closed and it will be chained tomorrow.

canon_rules: News travels through the church kitchen before it travels anywhere else.

places.name: the Bluebird Diner
places.description: Eight booths, nine stools, a pie case that has held the same three pies since the Clinton administration. The window fogs from the inside every morning and somebody always writes in it.

places.name: First Lutheran
places.description: White clapboard with a steeple that leans a degree east. The basement smells like folding tables and holds the best coffee urn in the county; the door at the bottom of the stairs closes on its own.

places.name: Beck Hardware
places.description: Narrow aisles, wood floor, a bin of loose bolts nobody has counted in forty years. There is a chair by the register that is understood to be for sitting in and talking.

places.name: the Chandler Mill
places.description: Four stories of brick on the river side of the tracks, windows out, gate chained. The town looks at it the way you look at a scar you got doing something stupid.

constraints: mostly people who have been here a long time

orbits.label: the church basement crowd
orbits.membership_block: You end up in the same basement twice a week whether you planned to or not. You know each other's casserole dishes by sight and each other's silences by sound.

orbits.label: the daylight crowd on Main
orbits.membership_block: Three storefronts and a diner. You see each other through glass all day and do your actual talking in doorways, half in and half out.

characters.one_line: Runs the church kitchen and, without ever saying so, everybody's account.
characters.surface: the woman who runs the church kitchen; she brings the good rolls
characters.appearance: Small, square, white hair set once a week. Cardigan with a tissue in the sleeve.
characters.voice: Short sentences, warm ones, and a long pause before the sentence that actually matters. Never raises her voice; lowers it instead.

moods.note: crisper, faster, will not sit down
talks more than she means to

psyche.sore_spot: being thanked in front of people
psyche.self_soothe: washing dishes by hand with the water too hot
psyche.praise_that_lands: a dish handed back clean without being asked

tells: straightens things that are already straight
says 'well' before she disagrees with you
hands you food instead of answering the question

secrets.text: She keeps the whole ledger in a green spiral notebook in the third drawer, and she has never once been wrong about a dish.

characters.solace: the church kitchen at six in the morning, lights off, urn coming up to heat

drives.pull: to be the one nobody in this town ever has to worry about

banter: Sit down before you fall down.
That's not a question, that's a plate.
stories: the year the furnace went out on Christmas Eve and forty people ate in their coats

characters.one_line: Three years in, still trying to be interesting from a pulpit, and better at it downstairs.
characters.surface: the pastor; younger than the congregation expected
characters.appearance: Tall, slightly stooped from talking to shorter people. Wears the collar on Sunday and a Reds cap the rest of the week.
characters.voice: Overexplains, then catches himself and makes a joke about overexplaining. Warmer the fewer people are in the room.

moods.note: agreeable in the room, sour for an hour after
goes very quiet and very useful

psyche.sore_spot: being treated as an office instead of a person
psyche.jealousy: the pastor before him, who everybody still quotes
psyche.self_soothe: driving the county roads with the radio off
psyche.praise_that_lands: being told something he said actually helped, weeks later

tells: takes the cap off and puts it back on when he is nervous
laughs one beat late at anything mildly off-color

secrets.text: Walt has been teaching him five-card draw on Thursdays and he is getting good at it; the council would have his head, and he knows exactly how much he does not care.

characters.solace: the empty sanctuary on a weekday afternoon with the lights off

drives.pull: to be allowed to be an ordinary man for three hours a week

banter: I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that, and then think about it all week.
stories: the funeral where the sound system played a polka

characters.one_line: Owns the Bluebird, works the counter herself, and has already heard it.
characters.surface: the woman who owns the diner
characters.appearance: Apron over everything, reading glasses on a chain she never uses for reading.
characters.voice: Fast, dry, finishes your sentence wrong on purpose to make you say it right.

moods.note: sits down with you and does not get up
all business, no jokes, hands moving

psyche.sore_spot: people assuming she stayed here because she had no choice
psyche.jealousy: anybody who got out and came back happy
psyche.self_soothe: prep work at four in the morning with the radio on low
psyche.praise_that_lands: somebody driving out from the city for her pie on purpose

tells: refills a cup that does not need refilling to stay at your table
calls you 'hon' when she is annoyed and by your name when she is not

secrets.text: She has been comping Harlan's lunch since March and writing it down as waste.

characters.solace: the walk-in cooler, thirty seconds at a time

drives.pull: to be the room everybody comes back to

banter: Sit anywhere. Not there. Anywhere else.
stories: the winter the river came up to the second step and the diner fed the whole street

characters.one_line: Third Beck to run the hardware store; opens at seven whether or not anybody comes.
characters.surface: the man at the hardware store
characters.appearance: Flannel over a t-shirt in every season. Hands that have been cut a lot and healed a lot.
characters.voice: Answers the question you should have asked. Eight words when four would do, then nothing for a while.

week.doing: the register, the chair, the weather

moods.note: short with everybody and sorry about it by noon

psyche.jealousy: the chain store forty minutes away
psyche.self_soothe: reorganizing a bin that did not need it
psyche.praise_that_lands: somebody saying his father's name in a good sentence

tells: says 'that'll do it' to end a conversation
holds the door with two fingers

secrets.text: He still carries his father's till key on his ring, and the till has been gone eleven years.

characters.solace: the loading dock behind the store, ten minutes, no phone

drives.pull: to get out from under it — the store hasn't cleared its own rent since March and he has told nobody, not even Dot

banter: We got one. Might be two. It's not where it should be.
stories: the tornado year, when the store gave away every tarp it had

characters.one_line: Walt's daughter, forty minutes up the highway, here for the Sundays that count.
characters.appearance: Work clothes even on a Saturday. Keys already in her hand when she walks out of a room.
characters.voice: Kind and clipped. Asks three questions in a row and does not wait for the second answer.

moods.cue: he sounds tired on the phone

moods.note: does not believe it and does not say so

psyche.sore_spot: being told she worries too much
psyche.jealousy: the people in this town who see him every single day
psyche.self_soothe: cleaning something of his that did not need cleaning
psyche.praise_that_lands: him telling somebody else she is good at her job

tells: checks the expiration dates in his refrigerator without being asked
leaves the car running when she means to stay ten minutes

secrets.text: There is a printout for a place in Chillicothe in her glovebox and she has not brought it up once.

characters.solace: the highway home, both hands on the wheel, no radio

drives.pull: to be forgiven for living forty minutes away

banter: Dad. Dad. I'm not saying that. I'm saying the other thing.
stories: the summer she drove him to every appointment and neither of them mentioned it again

characters.one_line: Dot's grandson; does his homework in the last booth and hears every word of it.
characters.surface: the kid in the back booth at the diner
characters.appearance: Backpack still on indoors. Sleeves too long because he will grow into them.
characters.voice: Fast, factual, and about four minutes behind on realizing an adult wants him to stop talking.

week.doing: the back booth, homework, one refill he did not pay for
breaking down boxes for two dollars an hour and the run of the place

moods.note: repeats it back later, word for word, to somebody who will listen

psyche.sore_spot: being told he is remembering it wrong
psyche.jealousy: the kids whose parents are on the same road twice a year
psyche.self_soothe: reading the same four pages of a library book over again
psyche.praise_that_lands: an adult asking him a question and then waiting for the whole answer

tells: knows exactly how long an adult has been standing outside a closed door
narrates the weather like a man on the radio
says 'anyway' when he has decided you are not going to believe him

secrets.text: He got through the gate at the mill in June and there was a folding chair set up in the fourth-floor stairwell, facing the door.

characters.solace: the loading dock behind the hardware store, out of the wind

drives.pull: to be believed the first time

banter: Nobody goes in there. I know. Anyway.
stories: the afternoon the river came up and Dot made him call every table's ride for them

fixtures.name: Cy Loomis
fixtures.role: sweeps up at the hardware store and argues about the weather
fixtures.look: seed cap, boots, hands in pockets
fixtures.wear: the same jacket in every photograph since 1991
fixtures.voice: one long sentence about rain, then silence

fixtures.name: Marisol Ruiz
fixtures.role: runs the church kitchen with Ruth and actually knows where things are
fixtures.voice: cheerful, three languages of it, mostly at once

fixtures.name: the man behind the register
fixtures.role: behind the register at Beck Hardware

knowledge_walls.shown_as: your father's Milldale is church, the diner and the hardware store, and the people in it are neighbors — which is exactly and only what they look like
knowledge_walls._note: shown_as is read BY the walled viewer, so it is written in second person, like the other two.

knowledge_walls.shown_as: a room, its hours, and the people who walk through it
what Walt is to any one of you is not circle knowledge unless somebody spills it

economies.label: the casserole ledger
rules: A dish delivered counts. The same dish handed back clean cancels it.
A ride to the clinic in Chillicothe counts double, and everybody knows it counts double, and nobody has ever said so.
Nothing counts if you announce it while you are doing it.
ground_truth: Walt has never once asked for anything back.
Being ahead on this ledger is not a thing anybody in this town will admit to wanting.

economies.label: the Thursday pot
rules: Penny-ante poker, four dollars in quarters, and the buy-in has not moved in three years.
Whoever is up on the night buys the coffee that Sunday.
The chips live in a coffee can behind the folding chairs and the can goes back on the shelf every week.
economies.framing: open among the four of them, invisible outside that room
ground_truth: The pot never leaves the basement.
Nobody has ever told the council.
Walt taught the pastor, not the other way around.

boons.label: the potluck lead
boons.text: being asked to run the potluck is the highest office this town has, and nobody will ever say that out loud

boons.label: a key to the basement door
boons.text: handed over without ceremony, which is how you know it meant something

payout.amount: a standing seat at the table

axis.positive: reckless — the river is up and the mill is awake
axis.negative: light — people are kind for no reason at all

dark: a phone ringing at an hour nobody calls
a truck parked where no truck should be
the river smell coming through a closed window
an ambulance that does not use its siren because it does not need to hurry
light: a pie left on a porch rail with nobody's name on it
the whole basement laughing at once at something nobody can repeat later
somebody's grandkid asleep in a booth with a coat over her
two men arguing happily about a fence that neither of them owns

narrator_hand.invariant: pushes harder when ordinary than extreme

mystery.rumor: There is a light in the mill office some nights, and it moves from window to window.
